newsitem.title: UK: London tube railway working fine after power loss.
newsitem.headline: London tube railway working fine after power loss.

text.p: London's underground train system was running normally on Thursday after the network was paralysed for 2-1/2 hours by a power failure on Wednesday night, a spokesman for the operators London Underground said.
"Everything is working normally. We have not had to cancel any services," he said by telephone.
Thousands of passenger were trapped in tunnels and stations when a boiler at the system's main power plant failed, although emergency lighting meant they were not left in the dark.
There were no reports of any injuries and the spokesman said passengers had remained calm during the blackout.
"Power stations do go down from time to time. The ideal world where things don't break down just doesn't exist," the spokesman said.

The stoppage brought chaos to London streets as bewildered tourists and residents left restaurants, cinemas and theatres and were faced with a long wait to travel home on a freezing night. Long queues built up for buses and taxis.
The underground network comprises 248 stations on 11 lines that criss-cross Europe's biggest city and transport 2.7 million people a day.
In April a power failure -- which officials then called the worst ever -- hit the Underground, trapping passengers in trains and causing chaos for Easter tourists and sports fans.
Passenger groups have warned the government that lack of investment in the Underground system could have serious long-term effects.
